tasks.short: Direct and apply signed changes to databases

steps.what: File requested changes from the analysts
Match requested objects to existing databases
Draft a reversible script for those changes

loop.input: request fields and the change template
loop.output: script draft that names only objects on the form
loop.check: Every object name in the script equals a form field
loop.stop: One draft, then blank any line with no object name
loop.why_not_simpler: Rollback wording varies by object and a fixed paragraph cannot write it

steps.what: Review the scan before any live changes
Sign the script and direct the programmers
Apply only that signed script on the database

tasks.design: Programmers and analysts submit object name, change type, reason and rollback on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft in {DOCS} writes the change script from those fields, then a scan lists issues for review. The database administrator signs one version in the direction meeting, and only that version is applied by the native job on {DATA_PLATFORM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change text lived in mail, so a draft could not show which object it would touch or who had accepted the rollback.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalog and the request form can share an object name, so each name in the script can be checked against a field.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a change is safe on live data is still a judgement. A clean scan is not proof the script is correct.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator accepts the rollback, directs the programmers, and signs the only version that may be applied.

ambition.what: Sign each database change when it is ready, not in a weekly batch

tasks.altitude: Less time rewriting scripts, more time refusing unsafe changes. The administrator can block an apply that has no signed version.

reach.task: Code only the change the administrator signed
reach.learn: Which object names were approved and which were sent back

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm a database change is a request, a script, a review and a signed apply. Directing programmers is still a conversation.
Digest [S4] says a coding assistant still needs a person to review what it writes, including a short change script.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe a small trial of experienced developers who were slower with a coding assistant while they felt faster, and a later rerun the authors called inconclusive.
Digest [S11] reports a large developer field study with more completed tasks and a wide error margin, with a larger effect for juniors.
Digest [S6] describes scanning of code and dependencies that still needs a person to review the fix.
Digest [S27] says models wrote vulnerable code in a large share of tests, so a clean scan is not proof the change is correct.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended live change is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The task ends when the signed script is applied or refused. Broader redesign is out.

Input contract: object name, change type, reason, rollback, requester. Producer is the programmer or the analyst. If the form is empty the administrator types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
Test the native change job and approval on {DATA_PLATFORM} before any custom runner. A passed check or a clean scan is not approval.
The prior puts much of this task in meetings. Directing programmers is that conversation. Matching objects and applying the signed script are console work.
unknowns: Who may sign when the administrator is absent.
Whether production writes are frozen outside a change window.
research_questions: How often is the requested object missing from the catalog?
How often is the first apply rolled back?

already_counted.description: Administrator rewrites weak rollback lines in the draft
Administrator's direction and sign-off on the script

incremental.description: Keep the change template aligned with new object types
Analysts resubmit forms the catalog check rejects

approvals.approved_version: change script version signed in this review
the same signed change script version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most requests still arrive as free text, so the script is rewritten by hand. The high case assumes clean forms but every live change still has a full sign-off. Time spent directing programmers is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Safeguard computer files with signed measures

steps.what: Read current controls on computer files
Hear risks of accidental or unauthorized damage
Draft security measures from the risk form

loop.input: risk fields and the measure template
loop.output: note that cites the store id and the risk
loop.check: The store id and the risk text match the submitted fields
loop.stop: One draft, then stop a section that has no store id
loop.why_not_simpler: Why a measure fits this store is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Check the log lists only security events
Sign measures against unauthorized disclosure
Apply the signed measures to those files

tasks.design: The administrator reads current controls on {DATA_PLATFORM}, then hears the store id and the risk from the information owner. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts security measures from those fields, including a log limited to event type, store id, time and outcome. The administrator signs one version, and only that version is applied. No view of how a named person works is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Risk notes and control screenshots lived in different places, so a draft could not show which file store it referred to.
tasks.enabler_now: The file store id can be shared between the control export and the risk note, so each measure can be tied to a field.
tasks.still_hard: Which risk is acceptable is still a judgement. Whether this firm owes a cyber duty of care depends on sector and size.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator decides which measures are enough and signs the only version that may be applied.

ambition.what: Re-check file safeguards every quarter, not only after an incident

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting screenshots, more time on the risk. The administrator can refuse a measure that has no store id or an open-ended log.

reach.task: Confirm the safeguard on their file store
reach.learn: Which measures were signed and which risks were left open

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is a control review, a risk conversation and a signed change to file safeguards. The hard part is the risk, not the formatting.
Digest [S16] and [S17] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care. Scope depends on sector and size.
Digest [S18] and [S19] say that, for firms in scope, the duty includes supply-chain and patching measures, and incident reports are due at 24 hours, 72 hours and one month.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to a live safeguard is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The task ends when the signed measures are applied or refused. Filing a regulatory incident report is a later task.

Input contract: store id, risk, proposed measure, owner, log fields. Producer is the information owner. If no form exists the administrator types the same fields from the meeting and marks the row manual.
Test native control settings and approval on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code. The log stores event type, store id, time and outcome only.
This design does not watch how a named person works, so it does not add staff monitoring.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
Who owns a file store that sits with a supplier.
research_questions: Which file stores have no named owner?
How often does the log contain fields nobody uses?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits the measure note where the risk is thin
Administrator's decision on which measures are enough

incremental.description: Keep the measure template and the allowed log fields current
Owners correct a store id the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: safeguard version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes risks arrive as prose, so the measure note is rewritten by hand. The high case assumes a clean store id but every safeguard still needs a signature. Incident reporting itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and install signed database upgrades

steps.what: Collect version and performance symptoms
List upgrade steps from the software note

loop.input: software note and the version field
loop.output: checklist of steps tied to the target version
loop.check: Each step cites a version that is written on the note
loop.stop: One pass, then leave the list blank if the note has no version
loop.why_not_simpler: Release notes are prose and a fixed table cannot list the steps

steps.what: Sign the install window for these upgrades
Install the signed software upgrades
Check database performance after the install

tasks.design: A {BI} view shows version and performance symptoms from {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded read of the software note in {DOCS} builds a checklist only where the note names a version. The administrator signs the window and the version. The native upgrade job installs only that version. Nothing installs unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Release notes and the performance view did not share a version id, so a checklist could not be tied to a symptom.
tasks.enabler_now: The platform can export the current version, and the note can be stored with that same version id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this window is safe for live use is still a judgement, even when the checklist is clean.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator picks the version, the window and the rollback, and can refuse the install.

ambition.what: Review the upgrade when performance slips, not only on the yearly date

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping the release note. The administrator still owns the window and can stop the install.

reach.task: Hold the business window the administrator signed
reach.learn: Which version was refused and which window was accepted

evidence.claim: Upgrades in a mid-size firm are rare and planned. Once the version and the window are signed, the install itself is a known platform job.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended upgrade of a live database is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The task ends when the signed version is installed or the window is refused.

Input contract: current version, target version, symptom code, window start, window end, rollback. Producer is the administrator from the platform export plus the note stored in {DOCS}. If the note has no version id the checklist stays manual.
Test the native upgrade job on {DATA_PLATFORM} before any custom runner. The job cannot start without the signed version.
The prior puts a large share of time in meetings. Collecting symptoms and installing are console work. Agreeing the window is the meeting.
unknowns: Whether the administrator may install during business hours.
Who signs when the administrator is on leave.
research_questions: How often does a release note lack a version id?
How often is the install rolled back?

already_counted.description: Administrator finishes checklist lines the note left unclear
Administrator's window decision before any install

incremental.description: Update the checklist headings when the platform adds a version field

approvals.approved_version: upgrade version and window signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes release notes stay unstructured, so the checklist is rewritten by hand. The high case assumes a clean note but the window decision and the post-check stay manual. No unattended install is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Specify access levels for each segment

steps.what: Request a segment and the access levels
Compare each segment of the database
Specify access levels for the named users
Grant the signed access on that segment
Write the grant log for these users

tasks.design: A team manager requests a person id, a segment id and a level on a {WORKFLOW} form. The administrator compares that request with the segment list on {DATA_PLATFORM} and specifies the level. Only the signed level is granted. The grant log in {DOCS} stores person id, segment, level, approver and time, and nothing else.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access asks arrived as copied lists in mail, so a grant could not be checked against a segment id.
tasks.enabler_now: The segment list and the request can share a segment id and a closed set of levels.
tasks.still_hard: Whether this person should have this level on this segment is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator specifies the level and can refuse the request. Nobody else may grant it.

ambition.what: Re-specify access when someone changes team, not only when a ticket arrives

tasks.altitude: Less time retyping names. The decision of who may read a segment stays with the administrator, and an unsigned grant cannot run.

reach.task: Request a level for a person on one segment
reach.learn: Which levels were refused and which segment ids were wrong

evidence.claim: Specifying access in a mid-size firm is a judgement for each segment. Once the level is chosen, recording the grant is repetitive.
Digest [S16] and [S17] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care. Scope depends on sector and size.

Digest [S18] and [S19] say that, for firms in scope, care includes supply-chain and patching measures, and incident reports are due at 24 hours, 72 hours and one month. Those reports are not this grant task.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A grant log of person, segment, level, approver and time fits that limit.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended grant on a live database is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the database administrator. The task ends when the signed level is granted or the request is refused.
Input contract: person id, segment id, requested level, reason, manager. Producer is the team manager. If the form is empty the administrator types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
Test native grant roles on {DATA_PLATFORM} before custom code. Levels are a closed list, not free text.
The prior is not meeting-heavy. The decision is made on the access screen. Grant totals by segment are not a view of how a named person works, so this design does not add staff monitoring.
unknowns: Whether leavers are removed by another task.
Who may specify a level when the administrator is absent.
research_questions: What share of requests names a segment that does not exist?
How often is the requested level reduced?

already_counted.description: Administrator checks segment rows that do not match cleanly
Administrator's decision on the level for these users

incremental.description: Keep the segment list and the closed set of levels current
Managers correct a person id or a segment id the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: access decision signed in this review
the same signed access decision for the log

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests stay as free text, so the administrator still interprets the level. The high case assumes clean forms but every grant is still a human decision. Removing access for leavers is a different task and is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator stops retyping change text, safeguard notes and access rows, and spends the week on what may change, which safeguard is enough, and who may read a segment.
reach: Programmers receive the signed change script instead of a mail thread.
Information owners receive the safeguard version that was applied to their files.
Team managers see the access level granted on each segment.
skills_to_grow: State a database change as a reversible script with an owner and a rollback.
Tie each file safeguard to a store id and a named risk before it is applied.
Choose an upgrade from performance symptoms and a signed window.
Grant access by segment and level, and log only that decision.
role.ambitious_version: Every live change, file safeguard, upgrade and access grant is a signed version, and nothing writes to production unattended.
